scenes.say: Two smart people each make the best move for themselves. Both lose. That's not a bug, it's math.
The prisoner's dilemma. Two players can't talk. Each chooses: cooperate, or betray.
Whatever the other does, betraying pays you more. So both betray.
Both cooperate: {r00} points each. Both betray: {nash_r} each.
scenes.big_label: total when both betray vs both cooperate
scenes.note: Classic illustrative payoffs; code finds the Nash equilibrium

scenes.say: That's a Nash equilibrium: nobody wants to switch alone, even though both could do better.
Individual logic doesn't add up to group logic. You need trust, contracts, or a repeated game.

takeaway: Individual logic doesn't add up to group logic. You need trust, contracts, or a repeated game.
